clue.text: Islander supplies fruit, splendid fellow

parts.note: a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn
A1 means first-rate, written here with the figure 1 as the letter I
Ian is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man from some island is supplying fruit and is a splendid chap.
explanation.walkthrough: AI is A1, 'first-class', with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Pacific state of Hawaii is an islander.

clue.text: Boundary marker? What a laugh!

definitions.meaning: a sunken ditch and wall marking the edge of a park without blocking the view

explanation.surface: Fencing a garden boundary? How funny!
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken fence on an estate edge, and an exclamation of amusement.

clue.text: Bridge player astride fine horse in Somerset resort

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West
astride means sitting on
super means excellent or fine
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A card player straddling a good horse in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: WESTON-SUPER-MARE is a seaside resort in the English county of Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the Bristol Channel coast of the county.

clue.text: Claim to be songwriter, one bringing in goods

parts.note: saying 'I'm ...' is claiming to be someone
Cole Porter was an American songwriter

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be a songwriter while really trading in foreign goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm Porter' is the claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who buys foreign goods into a country.

clue.text: One injecting poison to middle of nice meat jelly

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: middle of means only the central two letters of nice are taken

explanation.surface: A snake's venom goes into the centre of a pleasant savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes IC from the middle of 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear savoury gelatin made from stock, used to coat cold dishes.

clue.text: Married male appropriately clad for conference?

indicators.note: clad means dressed in, so the clothing word is wrapped round the two letters

parts.note: to suit is to be appropriate; being suitably dressed points to a suit

explanation.surface: A married man has dressed properly for a business meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter leans on SUIT and 'suitably', i.e. appropriately; the two Ms go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a top-level meeting between heads of government.

clue.text: Acceptance of offer the alert are quick on

definitions.meaning: the rate at which people take up something offered
being quick on the ... is grasping things fast

explanation.surface: Agreement to an offer is something sharp people grab quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Take-up of a scheme is one sense; understanding, as in being quick to understand, is the other.

clue.text: See goc blench — man had bomb in nato HQ

indicators.note: a bomb blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Look, a general officer flinched when a man set off a bomb at an alliance headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bomb' shuffles GOC BLENCH MAN HAD. 'See' is a link, telling the solver to look. GOC is General Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city housed NATO's Joint Headquarters for decades.

clue.text: Unlawfully enters Cheltenham, say, breaking locks

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the hair word to put another inside

parts.note: tresses are locks of hair
Cheltenham is an English spa town

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the locks to get into Cheltenham illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like door fittings but means hair; 'breaking' puts SPA into TRESSES. CHELTENHAM is a spa town in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: Going onto someone's land without permission.

clue.text: A body-builder circling rock

parts.note: a steroid is a drug that builds muscle

explanation.surface: A muscle man circling a boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body-builder' looks like a person, but it is a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet is a lump of stone orbiting the sun.

clue.text: English ships Poe represented as water carriers

indicators.note: represented means shown in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: English vessels are depicted by Edgar Allan Poe as carrying water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' shuffles E with SHIPS and POE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden hoses convey water from the tap to where it is needed.

clue.text: It may be perfect under pressure

definitions.meaning: in grammar the perfect is one form of a verb, like past or future
strained and nervous, as when stressed

explanation.surface: Something might turn out flawless even when strained.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is a grammatical form of the verb, and someone anxious and strained is described the same way.

clue.text: Go round most of Balzac's birthplace

indicators.note: most of means everything but the last letter of the place name is kept

parts.note: the novelist Balzac was born in the French city of Tours

explanation.surface: Visit nearly all of the French town where Balzac was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final S of TOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a circuit of somewhere visiting its sights is to go round it.

clue.text: Desk job naval ratings originally had in dock

indicators.note: in places the ratings and the letter inside the word for dock

parts.note: to dock a tail is to clip it short
erk is slang for a low-ranking sailor or airman

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the word had is used

explanation.surface: A sailors' office posting while their ship was in dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a harbour but is the verb, to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Working as a clerk is an office post at a desk.

clue.text: Made fantastic whip when in dire difficulty

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous, fantastic

indicators.note: in places the whip inside the shuffled letters
difficulty here means trouble, so the letters of dire are rearranged

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip

explanation.surface: A great whip was invented when things got really tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficulty' rearranges the letters of 'dire' into RIED, and 'in' sets the whip inside them; 'when' is only a link. 'Made' looks like part of the surface phrase but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufactured or constructed, as with things made from parts.

clue.text: Seaman's shelter no one backs, withholding vote

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, with the possessive S
a tent is a canvas shelter

indicators.note: backs means the words no and one are written back to front

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor's refuge that nobody supports, while a vote is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns NO + I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining to cast a ballot either way is abstaining.

clue.text: Het up about a river restaurant in china

indicators.note: about means placed around the letter a
up means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Agitated about a river eating place made of porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges 'Het' into TEH, and 'about' wraps that round A. 'china' looks like porcelain but is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A café serving tea, common in that country.

clue.text: Responsibility producing dividend, though not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the word's opening letter is left off

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment or dividend

explanation.surface: Duty that yields a payout, though not at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' removes the B of BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The burden of duty for something is the onus.

clue.text: Declare judaean hill an object of dislike

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: Proclaim that a hill in Judaea is something hated.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing one strongly hates is an aversion.

clue.text: Demonstrator ultimately liable to be carried away

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of demonstrator

parts.note: apt to do something means liable to do it

explanation.surface: A protester is in the end likely to be swept off by emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' picks R, the last letter of 'Demonstrator'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound and enraptured, wholly absorbed.

clue.text: Poor chap at university involved in farewell entertainment

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside the word for farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
U is the abbreviation for university
a poor devil is an unlucky fellow

explanation.surface: A hard-up student is caught up in a leaving show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' wraps the Latin farewell round the student letter and the unlucky fellow. 'Poor' reads as an adjective for the chap, but belongs to the phrase poor devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre with songs, sketches and acts was a popular entertainment.

clue.text: Go quickly up with master Pirrip's fruit

parts.note: Philip Pirrip, called Pip, is the hero of Great Expectations

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to nip is to dash

explanation.surface: Dashing up with a young gentleman's fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NIP into PIN. Pip, Philip Pirrip, narrates Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Possibly bear key composer used to let Novello in

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: to let a name in is to make room for it inside the composer's name
completes the phrase, letting the actor's name inside

parts.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor

explanation.surface: A tuneful composer lets the songwriter Novello into his work, perhaps a bear piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to let ... in' puts Novello's first name inside the composer's surname. 'Possibly' marks bear as just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear eats meat and is an example of a flesh-eater.

clue.text: Partly disembodied, it haunted Osbert's sister

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ghost haunted the Sitwell sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Osbert, Edith and Sacheverell Sitwell were a literary family.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Dame Sitwell was the sister of the writer Osbert Sitwell.

clue.text: Hamlet's forefathers were surely not so abrupt?

definitions.text: Hamlet's forefathers were surely not so abrupt?

parts.words: Hamlet's forefathers were surely not so abrupt?
parts.note: Gray's Elegy says 'the ... forefathers of the hamlet sleep', meaning rustic villagers, not Shakespeare's prince; the clue jokes that they were not curt

explanation.surface: Surely the Danish prince's ancestors were not so curt?
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's prince, but Gray's Elegy in a Country Churchyard speaks of the rough forefathers of a village (hamlet); the word also means abrupt or impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means unsophisticated and rustic in Gray's line, and impolite or curt today.

clue.text: Note in tin giving name of gun

indicators.note: in places the note inside the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note in a can tells the gun's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Heavily plod around cargo-boat

definitions.meaning: to walk with heavy steps over a distance
a ship with no fixed route that takes cargo wherever needed

explanation.surface: Lumber heavily about a freighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge heavily is one sense; the other is a merchant steamer without a regular schedule.

clue.text: Self-styled don is at assembly across island

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch over either side of the island letters
assembly means putting the letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: A self-proclaimed university teacher is at a meeting over on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' shuffles DON IS AT into SOIDANT; 'across' sets it round IS.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'calling oneself', used of a so-called expert or claimant.

clue.text: Eager European admitted colouring yarns

indicators.note: admitted means taken inside, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: dying to do something means being eager for it

explanation.surface: A keen European was let into the storytelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarns' looks like tales, but is wool being coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating wool with a tint changes its colour.

clue.text: Two outstanding features identifying toast

indicators.note: Two means the face part is written twice

parts.note: a chin is a feature of the face that sticks out

explanation.surface: Two prominent features on a face mark out a celebratory drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' means protruding, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery salute said when raising glasses.
